# Taking what most hold

<!-- Generated by tools/research/registry.py; edit the matching JSON record. -->

`taking-what-most-hold` · **recorded-checked** · theorem · F01 · [record](taking-what-most-hold.json) · [register](../../../../RESULTS.md)

> Each formation taking, at each sense, a form more than half the formations hold, where there is one, makes no form; two of three agree at once and one of two rests, so agreement under it still needs a break of symmetry.

<a id="laws--规律"></a>
## Laws

1. Counting the holders of a form at a sense, taking what most hold keeps a formation's form where no form has more than half, and every form after it was held before by some formation. (`Becoming.SharedCodes.holders`, `Becoming.SharedCodes.majority`, `Becoming.SharedCodes.majority_held`)
2. Three formations, two holding one form: all hold it after one step. Two formations holding different forms: taking what most hold changes nothing. (`Becoming.SharedCodes.Majority.three`, `Becoming.SharedCodes.Majority.two`, `Becoming.SharedCodes.Majority.odd_agrees`, `Becoming.SharedCodes.Majority.even_rests`)

<a id="conditions--条件"></a>
## Conditions

- No axiom; a finite list of formations; decidable equality of forms.

<a id="does-not-show--未表明"></a>
## Does not show

- That majority rule agrees from every start, or that any group follows it.

**Standard boundaries:** No ethical premise and no Lean axiom is used. · Contains no ethical predicate and evaluates neither arising nor ceasing. · Stated for discrete steps. · A law of the formal model; its correspondence to actual systems is a separate obligation. · Names follow the structural naming criteria and are adopted only where the statement has their exact meaning; readings are interpretations, open to revision. · A relation omitted by a weaker description does not refute the fuller account.
